# Color depth


The depth argument of `Graphics` and `Graphics3D` decides what the front and back buffer are made of, so that what is drawn on top of each other many times does not lose its small steps to rounding:

| Depth | Format of the buffers |
|---|---|
| 24 | R8G8B8X8: 8 bits for red, green and blue. The alpha channel is not used. |
| 30 | R10G10B10A2: 10 bits for red, green and blue, and 2 for alpha. |
| 32 | R8G8B8A8: 8 bits for each, with alpha. |
| 64 | R16G16B16A16: 16 bits for each, with alpha, as half precision floats (1 sign, 5 exponent and 10 mantissa bits), never integers. |

0 (the best there is) and 16 (a 16-bit mode in the original) give 32, and so does any other number, with a warning on the console. If the graphics card can't draw to the format that was asked for, the next smaller of the list is used, and a warning says so. Pixels are read and written the way the buffer stores them, with the alpha on top: `ReadPixel`, `WritePixel`, `ReadPixelFast`, `WritePixelFast` and the `CopyPixel`s take and give ARGB for 24 and 32, A2R10G10B10 for 30, and the upper 8 bits of each channel as ARGB for 64. `ReadPixel64`, `WritePixel64`, `ReadPixelFast64` and `WritePixelFast64` work with the channels as `Float16` variables (`ReadPixel64 x, y, buffer, Out red, Out green, Out blue, Out alpha`, `WritePixel64 x, y, buffer, red, green, blue, alpha`) and are never converted to an integer: the depth 64 stores half floats, so what is read is what is stored (values above 1 included) and what is written is stored as it is. The other depths give the value from 0 to 1 that their bits mean, and clamp what is written to 0 to 1. The `Long` that the two read commands return is the memory of the pixel (8 bytes for the depth 64, with the red half float in the lowest 16 bits, then green, blue and alpha; the 4 bytes of the stored word for the others). `LockedPixels` has 4 bytes for each pixel (the number of `ReadPixel`) or 8 for the depth 64 (the half floats as they are in memory), `LockedPitch` fits, and `LockedFormat` says 5 for A2R10G10B10 and 6 for R16G16B16A16. Textures and images always stay RGBA8, and `SaveBuffer`, `GrabImage` and `CopyRect` convert on the way. What is shown on the screen is always R8G8B8A8, because HDR is not supported: the wider buffers are converted when they are shown, with the noise of `Dither` if it is on, which hides the bands that the rounding to 8 bits would otherwise make.

Below, 100 see-through layers whose alpha grows from column to column are added on top of each other, once for each depth. With 8 bits per channel every layer rounds to 0 or to a whole step, and the ramp has few steps; with 30 and 64 bits the layers add up.

![The same 16 columns of 100 faint layers drawn with the depths 32, 24, 30 and 64, from top to bottom](media/graphics/color-depth-ramp.png)

`GraphicsDepth` says what the buffers have. `GfxModeDepth`, `DisplayDepth` and `DisplayModeDepth` always say 32, the mode lists have each size once instead of once per depth the display could show, and `GfxModeExists` and `GfxMode3DExists` do not look at their depth argument. `WBuffer` does nothing, because the depth buffer is the float one described in the depth buffer page.

![A gradient shown through gamma tables that squeeze it, without Dither (top) and with Dither in two frames after each other (middle and bottom), contrast enlarged](media/dither/before-after.png)
